claims.text: Yakiniku tare and marinades at this type of restaurant contain wheat-based soy sauce. The menu also includes okonomiyaki and hormone udon — both made with wheat flour. Cross-contamination risk is high across the kitchen.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (含む小麦) is the foundation of yakiniku dipping sauce and most marinades used here; no wheat-free soy sauce alternative has been mentioned.
Every item on the menu is meat or offal-based. There are no vegan dishes and the entire cooking surface and kitchen is devoted to animal products.

No information on dedicated fryers or separated prep surfaces is publicly available. The kitchen handles fried suppon, tempura-style preparations, and other wheat-using techniques across a shared kitchen.

Traditional Japanese soy sauce (shoyu, which contains wheat) is a foundational ingredient in kaiseki cooking — used in broths, marinades, sauces, and finishing. No wheat-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned anywhere on the official site or review platforms.

All courses are built around animal proteins (suppon, seafood, game, wagyu). Dashi is almost certainly katsuobushi (bonito flake) or similar fish/animal-based stock. No plant-based dashi alternative is indicated.

The official menu page notes that the omakase kaiseki course 'accepts ingredient requests and accommodates allergies/preferences' — but this must be communicated at the time of phone reservation. There is no online form or written allergy protocol described.
Fully private-room dining eliminates cross-contact from other tables and allows the chef to tailor each course to the group's stated needs.
Tempura is a core menu item and likely uses the same frying oil as other dishes. No dedicated gluten-free fryer is mentioned anywhere.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (含む小麦) is the default condiment throughout the menu. No wheat-free tamari or soy sauce alternative is indicated.
Fish-based dashi is standard in Japanese creative cuisine at this level. All known dishes contain eel or fish-derived ingredients.
No allergy menu, allergy awareness training, or allergy-friendly service is referenced on any platform. Diners with serious allergies should call ahead (079-288-7714).
Anago (conger eel) itself is naturally gluten-free when served raw or grilled without batter or sauce. Sashimi and plain-grilled preparations are the safest starting point for a GF inquiry.
No information is published about cross-contamination controls, shared equipment, or dedicated preparation areas for allergen-free cooking.

Miso (soy-based, handmade) and soy-derived protein products are used extensively. The specific type of soy sauce used — whether wheat-containing shoyu or wheat-free tamari — has not been disclosed in any published source. Macrobiotic philosophy favours traditionally brewed condiments, which typically contain wheat.
No animal products are used anywhere in the café kitchen; the entire menu is 100% plant-based, so vegan cross-contact from cooking is not a concern here.

The café explicitly states: 'Please note that our foods are not specified as allergy-free. Please let our staff know in advance if you have any allergies.' Customers with allergies are asked to contact the café before visiting.
Entire menu is 100% plant-based with no meat, fish, eggs, dairy, or honey — eliminating vegan cross-contact risk entirely.
All seasonings and ingredients are sourced from the on-site natural food shop and are certified organic, naturally farmed, or low-pesticide with no synthetic additives.
Some individual items — such as the tofu and rice flour gateau chocolat — are made with inherently gluten-free ingredients, though no GF certification or dedicated preparation claim is made.

name: イタリアン食堂 ピザマリア 姫路店 (Italian Shokudo Pizza Maria Himeji)

claims.text: All pizzas share a single wood-fired stone oven; wheat flour from dough will be present on the oven floor throughout service — cross-contamination for anyone avoiding gluten is unavoidable.
No soy sauce or Japanese dashi-based elements identified in the Italian menu, but standard Italian sauces and dressings have not been confirmed allergen-free.
Cheese, cured meats, and anchovies are used throughout the kitchen; vegan cross-contact risk is high and no vegan protocols were identified.

name: 居酒屋 遊膳 本店 (Izakaya Yuzen Honten)

claims.text: No allergen menu or GF protocol is documented. Tempura is offered and the fryer's dedication is unknown, making cross-contamination from wheat batter a real risk.
Standard wheat-containing shoyu is used throughout; no tamari or GF soy sauce alternative has been mentioned in any source.
The kitchen handles seafood, chicken, and other animal proteins continuously; no plant-only prep area is documented.
No allergy-handling protocol or allergen chart has been reported. Phone reservations are available (079-287-8872) and would be the appropriate channel to discuss dietary needs before visiting.
Menu is highly seasonal and made-to-order from daily-sourced local ingredients, which means the kitchen may be able to accommodate specific requests if contacted in advance.

name: 姫路おでん 地料理 居酒屋 じごろ小廣 (Jigoro Kohiro)

claims.text: Multiple tempura items are listed (conger eel tempura, lotus root tempura, yam tempura, octopus tempura, surume tempura, kisu tempura) indicating active wheat-batter frying; no separate fryer for gluten-free items is noted.

The signature Himeji oden is served with homemade ginger soy sauce; multiple dishes reference soy-based sauces, ponzu, dashi soy, and wasabi mayo — all made with standard wheat-containing shoyu. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative is mentioned.
Bonito-and-kombu dashi is used as the base broth simmered one to two days; it permeates the oden and likely touches most hot dishes. Fish, seafood, eggs, and meat are cooked throughout the kitchen.

No allergen menu, allergy inquiry system, or staff allergy-handling procedure is documented on any available source. Japanese communication will be required to ask questions, and the kitchen is unlikely to have protocols for celiac-safe preparation.

The restaurant is a small owner-operated counter with a focused menu, meaning staff likely have detailed knowledge of their ingredients and preparations — a Japanese-speaking diner may be able to get honest answers about specific dishes.

name: 貝屋 マルホウ (Kaiya Maruhou)

claims.text: カキフライ（小麦粉パン粉衣）がメニューの主力であり、同じ厨房でグリル・生食・揚げ物が並行して提供される。専用フライヤーの有無は非公開。小麦を使用しない浜焼き・生牡蠣との調理動線上の分離も未確認。
醤油・たれ類の使用が想定されるが、グルテンフリー醤油（タマリ等）の提供は公式サイト・各種予約サイトいずれにも記載なし。焼き貝に添えるタレに小麦含有醤油が使われる可能性が高い。
全メニューが海鮮ベース。植物性食材との分離調理の概念はこの業態では想定しにくく、ヴィーガン対応の実績・表記なし。
アレルギー対応・スタッフへの指示プロトコルについていずれの媒体にも記載なし。セリアック・重篤アレルギーの場合は来店前に電話（079-262-6325）で直接確認が必須。
生牡蠣・蒸し牡蠣・浜焼き（単品でソースなし）は本来グルテンフリーの調理法。水産会社直営で添加物を使わない素材重視のコンセプトは、シンプルに食べられる料理を頼む場合にはプラス材料。
